articles.title: DICT, CICC, and NTC being sued by tech advocates
articles.description: Philippine tech leader and advocates, supported by BetterGov.PH, filed a petition for certiorari and prohibition against Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) Secretary Henry Rhoel Aguda, Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) Executive Director Renato “Aboy” Paraiso, and National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) Commissioner Ella Blanca Lopez. They are asking the Supreme Court to invalidate the orders that led to the service disruption and stop agencies from imposing similar nationwide blocks without a court order. The Discord controversy Discord was temporarily made inaccessible in the Philippines after government authorities raised concerns about online safety and the use of digital platforms in connection with harmful or illegal activity. The block was subsequently lifted, but its brief duration did not end concerns about the precedent it could establish. The petitioners’ argument is not primarily about restoring Discord access—the platform has already returned—but about limiting the executive branch’s ability to restrict an entire communications service unilaterally. They contend that a nationwide platform block can affect lawful speech, work communications, gaming communities, educational groups, developers and small businesses that depend on such services. For many Filipino users, Discord is more than a gaming chat application. It is used by software-development teams, online classrooms, freelance workers, fan communities, open-source contributors and remote organizations. A blanket block can therefore have consequences beyond the content or accounts that authorities intend to target. At the center of the dispute is the question of whether administrative agencies can direct telecommunications providers to cut off access to a platform nationwide, or whether such an action requires a court’s intervention. A Supreme Court ruling could clarify the legal boundaries for future actions involving social-media networks, messaging services, gaming platforms and other digital services. Broader crackdown on platforms The Discord issue is occurring amid wider government pressure on major online platforms to improve child protection, content moderation and cooperation with Philippine authorities. The CICC recently directed Reddit and Discord to designate resident agents or local representatives in the Philippines. It also asked the platforms to explain their existing safety arrangements and provide implementation plans for stronger safeguards, faster response systems and age-assurance measures. The agency’s moves followed heightened public concern about harmful online content and incidents involving minors. DICT has also indicated that it could pursue legal action against Meta if the company does not sufficiently cooperate with government requests involving online safety. Officials said the agency would first give platforms an opportunity to respond before moving forward with a case. Government agencies face real challenges: online platforms can be used to distribute abusive material, facilitate scams, expose minors to harm or spread violent content. Authorities need ways to demand faster action from companies whose operations and decision-makers may be located outside the country. However, critics argue that shutting down an entire platform is an exceptionally broad remedy. A nationwide block may affect millions of users, including people who have no connection to the alleged illegal activity. From this perspective, the more proportionate approach would be targeted removal of unlawful content, investigation of responsible accounts, lawful preservation of evidence, and court-supervised restrictions where necessary. The case also matters for the country’s digital economy. Developers, online workers, startups, gaming communities and technology organizations increasingly rely on global platforms to communicate and collaborate. Clear rules would help them understand when access to those services could be restricted and what legal protections are available.

articles.title: Messi readies for final farewell in Argentina send-off
articles.description: BUENOS AIRES, Argentina (AFP) -- Lionel Messi will bring the curtain down on his glittering Argentina career on Tuesday with a farewell friendly against Benin that marks the dawn of a new era for the South American champions. After more than two decades of service to his country, the 39-year-old superstar will hand over the captain's armband for good as he makes his final appearance in the Albiceleste jersey at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires. Messi will be joined for his international swansong by 85,000 spectators and several of the teammates with whom he reached the pinnacle of football at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, alongside members of Argentina's emerging generation. The friendly marks a symbolic passing of the torch for a player whose international legacy includes a World Cup title, two Copa America crowns and the Finalissima. Messi also bows out as Argentina's record appearance-maker and leading scorer, with 125 goals in 207 games, as well as a record 68 assists. His farewell comes two and a half months after Argentina's ill-tempered World Cup final defeat to Spain in New Jersey, where Messi exited in tears after making little impression. "I gave it my all; I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are great young players coming up who deserve their chance," Messi wrote when announcing his international retirement in August. Messi remains under contract with Inter Miami until 2028, although following the death of his father, Jorge, two months ago, he revealed he may hang up his boots for good sooner than anticipated. - Friends reunited - Members of Argentina's 2022 World Cup-winning squad -- the players who delivered the country's third star -- and their families will join Messi for Tuesday's farewell against Benin, ranked 93rd in the world. Veterans of that Doha triumph such as Angel Di María, who retired from international football in 2024, will be there to witness the passing of the torch to a new generation charged with extending the Albiceleste's golden era. Several of the newcomers, including Franco Mastantuono and Leonel Flores, were not even born when "La Pulga" ("The Flea") made his Argentina debut in 2005 for a team whose history had for so long been dominated by Diego Maradona. "It's going to be an unforgettable day for everyone. Everyone wants to be at this match, and now it's just about enjoying it," Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said. Argentina's new generation has already shown what it can do without its captain, although nobody is pretending replacing a man regarded by many as the greatest footballer in history will be straightforward. "Collectively, we will try to fill the void left by Leo," said Scaloni, who is negotiating a contract extension after leaving his future unresolved following the World Cup defeat in July. Scaloni, who mastered the art of building the right supporting cast around Messi, will also say goodbye on Tuesday to 38-year-old vice-captain Nicolas Otamendi. Like Messi and Otamendi, midfielders Rodrigo De Paul and Giovani Lo Celso were called up solely for the Benin game, raising the possibility that neither will represent Argentina again. - New generation - Those certain to be involved, at least from the bench, include other veterans of the 2022 World Cup who will be the standard-bearers for Argentina after Messi: defender Cristian Romero, midfielders Alexis Mac Allister and Enzo Fernandez, and forwards Julian Alvarez and Lautaro Martinez. Tenacious centre-back Romero is set to inherit the captain's armband, first worn by Messi at the 2010 World Cup in South Africa. Goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez and Lautaro Martinez are next in the captaincy hierarchy. They have already begun to rally around Messi's heirs, who showed their appetite for success in Argentina's first game since the World Cup final, against Bolivia in Cordoba on Wednesday. Argentina swept the Bolivians aside 4-0, with young talents Nico Paz and Jose Manuel Lopez among the scorers. They followed that victory with a 7-0 rout of Burkina Faso at the Monumental on Saturday, with Mastantuono and Gianluca Prestianni scoring their first international goals. While Argentina's future is beginning to take shape, one small but symbolically significant question remains: who inherits Messi's number 10 shirt? "We won't give the number 10 to anyone until Leo's match takes place," Scaloni said. "After that, we'll see."
